name: Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity
definition: The **Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity** of $\mathcal{H}$ is the minimum worst-case number of equivalence queries needed to identify an unknown target in $\mathcal{H}$, when every proposed equivalence hypothesis must itself belong to $\mathcal{H}$.
graph_summary: Minimum worst-case number of equivalence queries when every proposed hypothesis is in the class.
origin_references: Equivalence queries in the exact query-learning model are introduced in \cite{angluin1988queries}; this parameter restricts the learner's equivalence hypotheses to $\mathcal{H}$.

monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\{000,001,010,100\}$ has proper equivalence-query complexity 1, by querying $000$; a counterexample identifies which singleton is the target. Its subfamily $\{001,010,100\}$ has complexity 2, since a rejected singleton proposal can be refuted at its own coordinate and eliminate only that proposal.

p_monotonic.proof: Run a proper equivalence-query learner for $\mathcal H$ against counterexamples restricted to the retained coordinates, replacing each proposed hypothesis by its projection. The projected proposal is proper; any projected counterexample is also valid for the simulated original learner. If the projected proposal is accepted, its projection is the target. Thus projection cannot require more queries.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
